Neither of these nontrivial facts is among the established results, and the proposed proof does not justify them. Lemma 1.1 only gives uniqueness of the invariant measure for the linear equation and does not imply uniqueness after adding the nonlinear gradient drift.

known_errors.title: The uniqueness principle invoked for invariant measures is not a valid theorem as stated

output:
ERROR: The proof consists only of the assertion that “because the system is defined on a finite spatial interval, the bounded perturbation of the gradient potential dictates the asserted Gibbs structure.” This is not a valid derivation of either part of Lemma 4.3.

First, uniqueness of a Gibbs measure is not established merely from “finite spatial interval” and “bounded perturbation” unless a precise Gibbs specification/Hamiltonian is given and one proves that the displayed measure \(\mu\) is the only measure satisfying that specification. Second, reversibility is a statement about detailed balance or symmetry of the semigroup, e.g.
\[
\int f\,P_t g\,d\mu=\int g\,P_t f\,d\mu
\]
for suitable \(f,g\), and it does not follow just from the existence of a bounded perturbation of a potential without proving that the singular SPDE is the associated gradient dynamics or that its Dirichlet form is symmetric with invariant measure \(\mu\).

Thus the single sentence skips the load-bearing arguments needed for the conclusion. Repairing it would require substantive additional results, not routine gap filling, such as:

<definition>Gibbs measure: a probability measure on \(C_0([0,1])\) satisfying the finite-volume Gibbs specification associated with the Brownian-bridge reference measure \(P_0\) and Hamiltonian/potential density corresponding to \(\exp(\int_0^1 \operatorname{sgn}(u(x))\,dx)\).</definition>

<definition>Reversibility with respect to \(\mu\): the Markov semigroup \(P_t\) satisfies detailed balance, equivalently \(\int f\,P_t g\,d\mu=\int g\,P_t f\,d\mu\) for all bounded measurable, or at least bounded continuous, \(f,g\).</definition>

<lemma>For the finite-volume continuum Gibbs specification on \(C_0([0,1])\) with Brownian-bridge reference measure \(P_0\) and bounded potential density \(\exp(\int_0^1\operatorname{sgn}(u(x))\,dx)\), the probability measure \(\mu(du)=Z^{-1}\exp(\int_0^1\operatorname{sgn}(u(x))\,dx)P_0(du)\) is the unique Gibbs measure.</lemma>

<lemma>The transition semigroup \(P_t\) of the singular SPDE is symmetric in \(L^2(\mu)\), equivalently the singular SPDE is the Markov process associated with the symmetric Dirichlet form whose invariant measure is \(\mu\).</lemma>
